content.title: About
content.content: The club sandwich on wheat is a classic multi‑layered sandwich made with toasted wheat bread, chicken breast, ham, bacon, lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise. It is popular in cafés and restaurants worldwide as a hearty lunch or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first club sandwich appeared in the early 1920s in the United States and quickly became a staple of many diners.
The traditional recipe uses three slices of bread, giving the sandwich a tower‑like appearance.
Wheat bread provides a softer texture and a slightly richer flavor compared with white bread.
Club sandwiches are often cut into four triangular quarters, each easily eaten with a fork and knife.
In some countries avocado or cheddar cheese is added for extra flavor.

items.title: Protein from chicken and ham
items.content: High‑quality protein supports muscle maintenance and aids recovery after physical activity.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain wheat bread
items.content: Whole‑grain wheat bread contains dietary fiber that helps digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Tomatoes and lettuce are rich in vitamin C, vitamin K and potassium, which support immune function and heart health.

items.title: Beneficial fats from bacon
items.content: In moderate amounts, bacon provides monounsaturated fats that can help maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: The balance of carbohydrates, protein and fat makes the sandwich a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham and bacon can be very salty, which is not advisable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fat levels
items.content: Bacon and mayonnaise are rich in saturated fats; excess intake may raise cholesterol.

items.title: Wheat allergy or gluten sensitivity
items.content: Those with celiac disease or gluten intolerance should use a gluten‑free bread alternative.

items.title: Caloric load
items.content: A club sandwich is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Bacon and chicken must be fully cooked to avoid salmonella or other bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is typically served cut into four triangular pieces. It can be eaten by hand, but in restaurants it is often eaten with a fork and knife. Add extra mayo or mustard to taste, and include fresh veggies for added juiciness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: If not consumed immediately, store the sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Bread may become soggy, so keep it separate from sauces when possible.
